rules.sentence: If there are no neurological deficits or instability, and no previous failed therapy, a conservative approach can be attempted.
Depending on the particular pathogen detected, the antibiotic regimen is adjusted accordingly (Table 8), although the emergence of resistance strains may complicate matters.
Penicillin ± ceftriaxone ± metronidazole (or other appropriate antimicrobial agents)
Vancomycin or linezolid as the main targeted agents; daptomycin as an alternative when susceptibility is confirmed
Ampicillin, clindamycin or penicillin (or other antibiotic as determined by susceptibility testing)
Carbapenems, or cefoperazone/sulbactam, or piperacillin/tazobactam, or cefepime
Culture-guided antibiotic therapy, most commonly third-generation cephalosporin (ceftriaxone) or a fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin) or ampicillin and chloramphenicol
Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, metronidazole, tetracycline, or clindamycin
Ceftazidime ± aminoglycosides, meropenem ± aminoglycosides, or ciprofloxacin
Carbapenems or aminoglycosides in combination with 3rd/4th generation cephalosporins
Isoniazid + rifampicin + pyrazinamide + ethambutol (standard tuberculosis treatment)
Surgical intervention may be needed in selected cases with osseous instability, abscess formation, pain refractory to medical therapy, or neurologic deficit
